name: China
summary: Four state-owned operators receive spectrum administratively from MIIT (no auctions). China Telecom and China Unicom share a joint 5G network on 3.5 GHz and 2.1 GHz; China Mobile and China Broadnet co-build 700 MHz and share 2.6 GHz.

operators.name: China Mobile
operators.legal: China Mobile Communications Group Co., Ltd.
operators.notes: Co-builds and operates China Broadnet's 700 MHz network (2021 agreement); shares 2.6 GHz with CBN.

operators.name: China Telecom
operators.notes: Shares its 5G RAN with China Unicom (3.5 GHz and 2.1 GHz co-build since 2019).

operators.name: China Unicom
operators.legal: China United Network Communications Group Co., Ltd.

operators.name: China Broadnet
operators.legal: China Broadnet Mobile Network Co., Ltd. (中广电移动网络有限公司)
operators.notes: Fourth licensee (5G licence June 2019). Spectrum licences transferred from China Broadcasting Network Corp. to its mobile subsidiary on 2022-05-30. Network built with China Mobile.

bands.label: 600 MHz
bands.note: Not an IMT band in China: 470–698 MHz is used for broadcasting; the digital dividend given to mobile is 700 MHz (B28). No operator holds 600 MHz (MIIT licensed-band statistics).

bands.label: 700 MHz FDD (B28/n28)
bands.note: China Broadnet licence 703–733/758–788 MHz (reissued to China Broadnet Mobile Network Co. on 2022-05-30). China Mobile co-invests and shares the network but the licence is CBN's.

blocks.notes: Licensed to China Broadnet (中广电移动); network co-built 1:1 with China Mobile, which operates and shares it (CMCC holds no 700 MHz licence of its own).
Remainder of APT 700 plan, not licensed to a public mobile operator.

bands.label: 800 MHz (EU B20 / Japan B18/19/26)
bands.note: Band 20 is not used in China. China Telecom's '800 MHz' CDMA/LTE/5G spectrum is 3GPP Band 5 and is shown under 850 MHz.

bands.label: 850 MHz FDD (B5/n5)
bands.note: China Telecom holds 2×11 MHz at 824–835/869–880 MHz; the upper part of B5 overlaps China's 900 MHz (E-GSM) plan. MIIT approved 5G re-farming in August 2023.

blocks.notes: Ex-CDMA spectrum (awarded 2008); MIIT approved re-farming for 5G in Aug 2023.

bands.label: 900 MHz FDD (B8/n8)
bands.note: China Unicom edges confirmed by the MIIT re-farming approval; China Mobile's 889–904/934–949 MHz from secondary sources only.

blocks.notes: Used by GSM-R (China Railway), not a public mobile licence (from background knowledge, not source-verified).
GSM/LTE/NB-IoT; MIIT allowed 5G re-farming of CMCC's sub-3 GHz bands on 2024-12-31.
MIIT approved re-farming for 5G in Nov 2022 (edges confirmed in the approval).

bands.label: 1.4/1.5 GHz
bands.note: No public mobile operator holds 1400–1500 MHz spectrum (MIIT licensed-band statistics list none). 1447–1467 MHz is used for government/private TD-LTE networks (from background knowledge, not source-verified).

bands.label: AWS 1.7/2.1 GHz
bands.note: AWS band plan not used in China; 1710–1785 MHz is the Band 3 uplink.

bands.label: 1800 MHz FDD (B3/n3)
bands.note: All three incumbents confirmed as 1700/1800 MHz licensees by MIIT (April 2024 statistics); block edges from secondary sources.

blocks.notes: GSM/LTE
GSM/LTE
LTE

bands.label: PCS 1900 / 2 GHz AWS-4
bands.note: PCS/AWS-4 band plans not used in China; 1880–1920 MHz is TDD (B39) and 1980–2010/2170–2200 MHz is MSS.

bands.label: 1.9 GHz TDD (B39)
bands.note: China Mobile's F band. MIIT lists CMCC as the only 1900 MHz TDD licensee; secondary sources give 1885–1915 MHz in use.

blocks.notes: Not used by CMCC (reported as ceded/guard)
TD-LTE 'F band'; LTE anchor for 5G NSA

bands.label: 2 GHz TDD (B34)
bands.note: China Mobile holds 2010–2025 MHz (MIIT lists CMCC as the 2000 MHz TDD licensee).

blocks.notes: Ex-TD-SCDMA 'A band', TD-LTE

bands.label: 2100 MHz FDD (B1/n1)
bands.note: China Telecom 2×20 MHz and China Unicom 2×25 MHz, contiguous 2×45 MHz used for a shared 5G carrier since MIIT's 2021 n1 technical rules. Edges from secondary sources; amounts confirmed by press.

blocks.notes: Ex-3G spectrum; used for shared CT/CU 5G (2021 MIIT n1 rules)
Ex-WCDMA; shared CT/CU 5G

bands.label: 2300 MHz TDD (B40/n40)
bands.note: Indoor TD-LTE band. MIIT lists CMCC and CU as 2300 MHz licensees.

blocks.notes: TD-LTE (indoor)
TD-LTE 'E band', indoor use
Assigned to China Telecom for TD-LTE in 2013, but MIIT's April 2024 list no longer shows China Telecom in 2300 MHz; status unclear.

bands.label: 2.6 GHz TDD (B41/n41)
bands.note: China Mobile holds 2515–2675 MHz (160 MHz) since the December 2018 5G allocation.

blocks.notes: 160 MHz: 2515–2615 MHz 5G NR, 2615–2675 MHz TD-LTE. Includes 2555–2575 (ex-CU) and 2635–2655 (ex-CT) re-assigned to CMCC in Dec 2018. Shared with China Broadnet under the 2021 co-build agreement.

bands.label: 3.5 GHz TDD (n78)
bands.note: China Telecom 3400–3500 MHz and China Unicom 3500–3600 MHz (December 2018 5G allocation; 10-year licences issued 2020). The two operators run a jointly-built, shared network across the whole 200 MHz, but each licence is 100 MHz.

blocks.notes: Co-built and shared with China Unicom (single 200 MHz shared RAN)
Co-built and shared with China Telecom

bands.label: 3.3 GHz TDD, shared indoor (n78/n77)
bands.note: 3300–3400 MHz is licensed jointly to China Telecom, China Unicom and China Broadnet for 5G indoor coverage. Shown as a nominal one-third share each so that totals count the 100 MHz once.

bands.label: 4.9 GHz TDD (n79)
bands.note: China Mobile 4800–4900 MHz (2018); China Broadnet 4900–4960 MHz.

blocks.notes: Not assigned to public mobile operators
Trial licence Jan 2020; commercial licence reissued to China Broadnet Mobile 2022-05-30 for 4900–4960 MHz.
Some sources say CBN holds 4900–5000 MHz; the licence wording quoted from MIIT is 4900–4960 MHz.

bands.label: Upper 6 GHz (n104)
bands.note: No operator licence. 6425–7125 MHz is designated for IMT (MIIT 2023 allocation-table revision; from background knowledge, not source-verified). In May 2026 MIIT granted a 6G trial-frequency licence for 6425–7125 MHz to the IMT-2030 (6G) Promotion Group, not to operators.

bands.label: 26 GHz (n258)
bands.note: No commercial licences. MIIT granted the first 26 GHz 5G mmWave trial frequencies to operators (incl. China Mobile) in January 2025 for the Harbin Asian Winter Games; commercial assignment not yet made.

bands.label: 37–43.5 GHz (n259/n260)
bands.note: Not assigned; only trial/R&D use reported (39 GHz discussed as a secondary mmWave band).

bands.label: 47 GHz (n262)
bands.note: Not identified or assigned for IMT in China.

notes: All spectrum is assigned administratively by MIIT; there are no auctions. MIIT issued 10-year 5G licences for the mid-band 5G spectrum in 2020, and has since allowed re-farming of 2G/3G/4G bands for 5G (China Unicom 900 MHz Nov 2022, China Telecom 800 MHz Aug 2023, China Mobile sub-3 GHz Dec 2024).

Network sharing: China Telecom + China Unicom run one shared 5G RAN on 3400–3600 MHz and 1920–1965/2110–2155 MHz; China Mobile + China Broadnet co-build 700 MHz (CBN licence) and share 2.6 GHz. Blocks are shown under the licensee.
3300–3400 MHz is licensed jointly to CT, CU and CBN for indoor 5G; totals count it as one-third each.
China Broadnet's 4.9 GHz: the licence text (as quoted by Wikipedia and 21jingji from MIIT) is 4900–4960 MHz; some provincial and trade sources say 4900–5000 MHz. The licence wording is used here.

MIIT's April 2024 statistics of licensed bands (the regulator's list) name the bands per operator but not the frequency edges. Edges for 900 (CMCC), 1800, 1.9/2.0 GHz TDD, 2100 and 2300 MHz come from secondary compilations and are marked unverified.
missing: Regulator-published block edges for 900 (CMCC), 1800, 1900/2000 TDD, 2100 and 2300 MHz: not found in MIIT documents; secondary sources only.
China Telecom's 2370–2390 MHz (2013 TD-LTE assignment): no longer on MIIT's April 2024 list; whether it was formally returned could not be confirmed.
900 MHz 885–889/930–934 MHz GSM-R use and 1447–1467 MHz private TD-LTE: from background knowledge, not source-verified.
MIIT 2023 designation of 6425–7125 MHz for IMT: from background knowledge, not source-verified (the 2026 6G trial licence is sourced).
